reasoning: The document lays out a fairly comprehensive set of success measures - apprenticeship starts by level and function, diversity data, People Survey engagement scores, employer surveys on reduced contingent labour and productivity, external recognition by 2018, retention after completion, and levy spend. It also describes a process for developing and collecting this data: 'the Civil Service is undertaking a detailed data collection, which will be collected on a quarterly basis', coordinated by Cabinet Office, with a baseline being established and 'internally reviewed at the end of the financial year 2016/17', then 'monitored on a financial yearly basis'. This goes beyond simple success measures to describe an evaluation timetable and governance ('the Cabinet Office will maintain clear governance and a structured approach...which assures senior and line manager engagement and accountability'). This reaches level 2, as it gives comprehensive measures and some evaluation timetable. However, there is no mention of testing the policy first, no explanation of why testing is inapplicable, and critically no statement on publication of results - it says data will be used 'to inform and evaluate policy' but doesn't specify what happens to results or whether they'll be published externally. This falls short of level 3's requirement for clarity on publication plans and reasons for evaluation choices. To reach level 3, the document would need to explain why this particular evaluation approach was chosen and commit to publishing the findings on a clear timetable.
